title: The right dg-module homotopy quotient and standard cone structure
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For an associative unital differential graded integer algebra $A$, use its right dg modules, underlying complexes, shifts with unchanged right action, and signed cones from [def-sfb-dg-derived-category]. Two dg module maps $f,g:M\to N$ are homotopic if there is an additive degree-$-1$ right $A$-linear map $h$ with $f-g=d_Nh+hd_M$. Define $K(A,d)$ to be the quotient of the category of right dg modules by this relation, and $q$ its quotient functor. Let $\mathcal E(M)$ mean that the underlying complex of the module representing $M$ has zero cohomology in every integer degree. A standard homotopy pretriangulation datum consists of the underlying additive structure on dg modules, its quotient additive structure on $K(A,d)$, a zero object, additive integer shifts, and a pretriangulation [def-weil-triangulated-category]. It includes functors $H^n$ with $qH^n$ equal to underlying cohomology, existence of right dg shifts and cones with the specified underlying complex and action, and shift isomorphisms $q(M[n])\cong q(M)[n]$ natural on dg maps. Its distinguished triangles are precisely the triangles isomorphic to $q(M)\xrightarrow{q(f)}q(N)\xrightarrow{q(i)}q(C(f))\xrightarrow{-q(p)}q(M)[1]$, using those shift identifications. This defines the datum without asserting its existence or the octahedral or acyclic-subcategory axioms.
